title: Microsoft Teams: customise the recording and transcription notification text
summary: The briefing correctly reports the roadmap and the documented meeting notification controls. However, its summary promises no change without administrator action despite an unpublished default, and its checklist incorrectly suggests calling policies determine which meetings display custom text. The licensing section also overlooks the published general Teams licence requirement.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default value of the custom notification toggle for meeting or calling policies.
claims.quote: Searched: EnableRecordingAndTranscriptionCustomMessage default; recording-transcription-custom-message default group calls. Read the feature page and meeting/calling parameter excerpts: enable/disable instructions and parameter Default value: None, not a service default.

claims.where: summary versus front matter: defaultState and Why it matters
claims.claim: The summary promises that nothing changes until an administrator sets it, while the page reports the arrival default as unknown.
claims.quote: summary: "nothing changes until an admin sets it"; defaultState: "unknown"; Why it matters: "Microsoft has not stated whether the setting is on or off by default".
claims.fix: Replace the summary with: "IT admins can replace part of the recording and transcription notification text Teams shows participants. The roadmap status is Launched; Microsoft has not stated the setting's default, and Learn says custom messages are not supported in 1:1 calls." Keep defaultState as unknown.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no feature-specific licence entitlement is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes and the broad entitlement gap in Cost and licensing and Open questions with: "A Teams licence is required to use Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously. No additional licence requirement specific to custom notifications is published at the time of writing (November 2026)." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. This is the standard's product-level licensing understatement, not evidence of a published feature-specific licence.
